clue.text: Soldiers in play about capturing second in command

indicators.note: capturing means one piece takes the other inside it
about signals that the word for play is turned round

parts.note: to play is to sport, as in children sporting on the beach

indicators.note: second in asks for the second letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Troops are acting in a play whose plot involves seizing a deputy commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SPORT into TROPS, and 'capturing' puts O, the second letter of 'command', inside it. 'Second in command' looks like a deputy but only supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops is the ordinary plural word for soldiers serving in an army.

clue.text: Office worker casually visiting old city to get a deep-fried dish

parts.note: a temp is an office worker hired casually, on short contracts
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A temporary secretary tours an ancient city and is served fried food.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is the Japanese dish of seafood or vegetables fried in light batter.

clue.text: Old rag changed to new newspaper

indicators.note: changed means the letters of rag are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tired old tabloid has been relaunched as a fresh newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' gives RGA. 'Rag' is itself slang for a newspaper, a decoy here.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a periodical that speaks for a party or body, so a newspaper can be one.

clue.text: Bull-baiter told to choose a way in

indicators.note: told means the phrase is spoken, and the answer is what is heard

parts.note: to choose a way in is to pick a door

explanation.surface: A bullfighter is instructed to select an entrance to the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'told' signals that PICK A DOOR, said out loud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A picador is the horseman in a bullfight who goads the bull with a lance.

clue.text: Rebellion contained by gun restrictions

indicators.note: contained by means the answer sits inside the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A rebellion is held in check by firearms laws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contained by' points to the letters running across 'gUN RESTrictions'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrest is public discontent or disturbance, which can amount to a rebellion.

clue.text: Tongue almost twisted around a sweet

indicators.note: around means the jumble encloses the letter a
twisted means the remaining letters are jumbled
almost means the word tongue loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A tongue curls itself around a piece of candy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TONGUE to TONGU, 'twisted' rearranges it, and 'around' wraps the result round A to give N O U G A T.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of sugar or honey with nuts.

clue.text: Mexican dish and Indian dish served up in English-designed china

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
designed means the letters of china are arranged into a new pattern
served up, in a down clue, means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: dal is a dish of spiced lentils

explanation.surface: Mexican and Indian food are both brought out on fine English crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' gives NCHIA and 'served up' gives LAD, which 'in' places before the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a tortilla rolled round a filling and baked in chilli sauce, a staple of Mexican cooking.

clue.text: Syrup from plant with a caramel coating inside

indicators.note: inside means the a plus the caramel edges go within the plant word

parts.note: a tree is a plant

indicators.note: coating means only the outside letters of caramel are used

explanation.surface: A syrup is made from a plant, with a layer of caramel within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coating' takes C and L from the outside of 'caramel'; with A they go 'inside' TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is the dark syrup left from refining sugar, known as molasses in America.

clue.text: Fear surrounding money and experimental methodology

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for fear goes round the other pieces

parts.note: terror is extreme fear
the rial is the currency of Iran and other countries

explanation.surface: Nervous researchers are afraid of what money and experiments involve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' splits the fear word after its first letter. 'Fear' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Trial and error is the method of trying things repeatedly until one succeeds, an experimental approach.

clue.text: Unpleasantly satisfied when turning sticks

indicators.note: turning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: gums are adhesives, things that stick, and to gum is to stick

explanation.surface: Someone becomes self-satisfied when the tables turn in their favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses GUMS, read from 'sticks' as the verb meaning glues.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes a self-satisfied, complacent person, which others find unpleasant.

clue.text: Run into vehicle with relatives' jewels

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
uncles are relatives

explanation.surface: Someone crashes into a car carrying their family's jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' places the run letter after the second letter of the vehicle. 'Run into' reads like a crash, but the words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a red gemstone, especially a garnet cut in a rounded shape.

clue.text: Boy inhaling pot suddenly felt sick

indicators.note: inhaling means one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name
an urn is a large pot or vessel

explanation.surface: A young man smokes cannabis and is promptly nauseous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inhaling' is the containment signal. 'Pot' suggests drugs but is just a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: When the stomach turns, a person suddenly feels queasy, so the verb here means became nauseated.

clue.text: In case of emergency, put a drain to part of foot

parts.note: to tap is to draw off liquid, so a drain
an inch is a twelfth of a foot as a length

explanation.surface: An instruction to fit a drain next to a section of the foot, in an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of foot' looks anatomical but means the unit of length, a twelfth of a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: At a pinch is an idiom meaning if really necessary, when there is no better option.

clue.text: Wild West Indian right for daughter

indicators.note: right for daughter means one letter is swapped in place of the other

parts.note: a Barbadian is someone from Barbados in the West Indies

explanation.surface: A West Indian character in a Western story stands in for his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps R in place of D in BARBADIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarian used as an adjective means uncivilised and savage, as untamed as wild.

clue.text: Social worker screening calls by Australian in part of the North Pacific

indicators.note: screening means the bee word hides the other piece inside it

parts.note: a bee is a worker in a social colony
to ring is to telephone, so rings are calls

explanation.surface: A social worker screens telephone calls from an Australian in a remote northern posting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a care professional but is the insect; 'screening' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bering Sea lies between Alaska and Siberia, forming the northern arm of the Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Weak fellow fleeing fire

indicators.note: fleeing means that letter runs away from the word

parts.note: a flame is fire

explanation.surface: A feeble man runs away from a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleeing' removes F from FLAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame excuse or effort is a weak, unconvincing one.

clue.text: Poet losing son in stream

indicators.note: losing means that letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet

explanation.surface: A poet who has lost his son wanders by a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops S from BURNS. A burn is the Scottish word for a stream, apt for Burns.
explanation.definitionFit: A burn is a Scottish and northern English word for a small brook or creek.

clue.text: Bird flapping round horse upset robber

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the other piece
flapping means the letters of bird are tossed about
upset, in a down clue, means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A bird flapping its wings around a horse frightens a highwayman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapping' gives BRID, 'upset' gives GAN, and 'round' puts the first round the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit, one of a gang robbing travellers in wild country.

clue.text: Parents turning to furniture that's easily modified

indicators.note: turning means the pair is read backwards

parts.note: pa and da are both words for a father, so two parents
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Parents take up a piece of furniture that converts easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses PA + DA into ADAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Adaptable means able to be changed to suit new uses or conditions.

clue.text: People in bed get nothing as hot food to eat

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pit is slang for bed
men are people
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: People in bed are given nothing spicy to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal; the bed is the slang sense, as in 'get out of your pit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimento is a pepper, a capsicum, and also allspice, both used to add heat and flavour.

clue.text: Local leader deserved to be educated

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word local

parts.note: earned means merited, deserved

explanation.surface: A local councillor earned the right to be schooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes L from 'Local'.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned describes someone scholarly, having much knowledge from study.

clue.text: American stirred malty sedative

indicators.note: stirred means the letters of malty are mixed up

explanation.surface: An American mixes a malty drink that makes one drowsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' gives MYTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Amytal is a trade name for amobarbital, a barbiturate drug used to calm and induce sleep.

clue.text: Unsuitable term for skinflint carrying no money

indicators.note: carrying means the miser word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a miser is a skinflint

explanation.surface: Calling a skinflint generous is wrong, since he carries no cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' splits the skinflint word after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A misnomer is a wrong or inaccurate name applied to something.

clue.text: River to fill moat damaged by king's gun firing shells

indicators.note: to fill means the letter goes inside the jumbled letters
damaged means the letters of moat are knocked about

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A river floods a castle moat damaged by the king's artillery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges MOAT to MOTA, and 'to fill' puts R inside it to give MORTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortar is a short cannon firing shells at high angles.

clue.text: Go over head of corn during harvest

indicators.note: during means the letter comes inside the harvest word

parts.note: to reap is to harvest

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word corn

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect an ear of corn while gathering in the crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives C, which goes inside REAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise again, going back over the main points.

clue.text: Graduates almost fix letter in Old English to instrument

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to set is to fix
thorn is the runic letter for th used in Old English

explanation.surface: Graduates nearly finish setting a letter in an Old English text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts SET to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset horn is a tenor member of the clarinet family, a woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Rabbit trick with funny ending

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle

indicators.note: ending means the last letter of the word funny

explanation.surface: A rabbit pulls a prank that ends amusingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' gives Y, the last letter of 'funny'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cony, or coney, is an old word for a rabbit, still used for its fur.

clue.text: Lead widespread in the outskirts of Derby is very dangerous

indicators.note: in means the scattered letters go inside the other piece
the outskirts of means the outer letters of the word Derby
widespread means the letters of lead are scattered

explanation.surface: Lead pollution has spread around the edge of Derby, an English city, and is hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'widespread' gives EADL, and 'in' puts it between the outskirts of 'Derby'. 'Lead' looks like the metal or a verb but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly means likely to cause death, so extremely hazardous.

clue.text: Danced beginning and end of bolero with retired film star

indicators.note: beginning and end of means the first and last letters of bolero
retired means the name is turned back

parts.note: Johnny Depp is a film star

explanation.surface: Someone danced the start and finish of a bolero with a film star who has quit acting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns DEPP into PPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To bop is to dance to pop music, so bopped means danced.
